g.text: From alarm stream to actionable information
Exposed to the full RDF alarm stream
Technical or physiological conditions invalidate alarm
Multiple alarms convey the same underlying meaning
silence HR low while HR extr. low lasts
Combination of alarms reveals higher-level clinical meaning
Fig. 1 | MDA proof-of-concept: contextual reasoning over alarm-derived situational knowledge. Per-patient alarms are ingested, enriched using the MDA semantic framework, and continuously
reasoned over with clinical context. Reasoning outputs are classified into three categories—likely false positives, likely redundant information, and emergent combined meaning—to inform
patient-centered alarm management. Worked examples (A–C) are regression cases of the proof-of-concept rules. In device-centered alarm management, clinicians are exposed to the full RDF alarm
stream, whereas in patient-centered alarm management they are exposed to fewer, contextualized alarms and interpretations.
